rounds.fact: Suck.com pioneered a sarcastic, link-heavy, first-person writing style that influenced blog voice for years, despite the site itself shutting down back in 2001.
Friendster launched in 2002 and is widely credited as one of the first mainstream social networks, predating both MySpace and Facebook, before its own popularity overwhelmed its servers.
LAUNCH (later LAUNCHcast) was one of Yahoo's earliest music properties, offering personalized internet radio years before Pandora or Spotify existed.
The New York Times went online in 1996 and required free registration from the start, a controversial-at-the-time model that foreshadowed the paywalls most news sites use today.
Digg pioneered the user-voted news-aggregation format years before Reddit took over that space, and a single controversial 2010 redesign is often cited as the reason it lost most of its audience.
